sentence: The finding's quoted gate text and the --compliance override do not exist in document.md, so the quoted text does not exist as quoted and no implementer following the document builds a wrong gate.
evidence: Grep for compliance, tier and override in document.md returns no matches; the finding cites SPEC:121 and INV-B:199, which are not gate text in this document.

sentence: An implementer who writes an orca orchestration example into WORKER-CONTRACT.md as SA-2 permits then fails AC-C1, but that needs the assumed example; the literal backslash-pipe makes AC-C1 vacuous rather than impossible to pass.
evidence: Line 147 (SA-2): 'The only allowed mention of Orca in a changed command is as an example ... inside the contract file.' Line 158 (P0) adds src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md. Line 172 (AC-C1): grep -rnE with '(orchestration\|worktree\|terminal\|agent)' and 'prints nothing'.

sentence: An implementer who follows the load row (report 'none', 'P1 (usage line only)') and the Decisions row builds a load change with no Unattended mode section naming return-contract.yaml, and that is wrong because AC-1.1 requires that section for every command in sections 3.1-3.2, which includes load.
evidence: Line 112 (load row): 'Report (WC-4): none (see note)' and 'P1 (usage line only)'. Line 265 (Decisions): 'a report file would be an unrequested addition. Only its usage-line defect is fixed.' Line 195 (AC-1.1): 'every command in sections 3.1-3.2 has a ## Unattended mode section naming return-contract.yaml'. Line 159 (P1) lists load (usage line only).

sentence: An implementer following WC-3 may ask once and resume, but the text says 'may', leaves 'once' undefined for multi-gate commands, names no flag for the tdd, recommend and review-translation answers, and sets no wait limit; these are missing or undefined requirements, so no contradiction or impossible criterion follows.
evidence: Line 61 (WC-3): 'the session may instead ask the coordinator once ... then re-invoke or resume the command with the answer as a flag. On an ask timeout it resumes the same message ID'. Line 90 (tdd row), line 115 (recommend row), line 117 (review-translation row) name no answer flag.

sentence: An implementer who follows R9 writes a one-line summary to the audit log; the finding's wrong outcome (the line should carry deleted-row counts) needs a field list the document never states, so it is an unspecified detail, not a contradiction or impossible criterion.
evidence: Line 17 (R9): 'The nightly purge job runs at 02:00 UTC and writes a summary line to the audit log.' No field list for the summary line appears anywhere in document.md.

sentence: An implementer who follows section 4 and section 2.3 builds no pre-dispatch version check and no refusal line for coordinator-only commands; the document never requires either, so the wrong outcome depends on a requirement the document does not state.
evidence: Line 128 (section 4): 'These six are never dispatched as workers and get no --unattended mode.' Line 73 (section 2.3) lists what the brief carries; neither section mentions a version or support check.

sentence: An implementer who follows R13 keeps card numbers out of the ledger and logs, and R14 lets support staff view the full number on screen; R13 restricts writing to ledger and logs, not display, so the full-number screen only needs the added assumption that the number is stored locally.
evidence: Line 27 (R13): 'Card numbers are never written to the ledger or to logs; only the last four digits may be stored.' Line 28 (R14): 'Support staff may view the full card number of a charge when a customer asks for it by phone.'

sentence: An implementer must choose between a 13-command and a 37-command reading of P1 before building, so the wrong outcome needs a guess about which reading is meant; no stated text is directly contradicted without that guess.
evidence: Line 159 (P1 scope): 'the --unattended flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2'; its Commands column names 13 commands. Line 195 (AC-1.1) requires the section for every command in 3.1-3.2; line 196 (AC-1.2) says 'each P1 command'.

sentence: An implementer who follows R13 drops security alerts at the SMS limit; calling that wrong needs a safety exemption the document never states (R9 sets priority urgent and R10 covers only delivery failure), so the claimed breach rests on an unstated premise.
evidence: Line 16 (R9): 'Security alerts are priority urgent.' Line 15 (R8): 'Notifications above the limit are dropped without being queued.' Line 24 (R13): 'security alerts are dropped like any other notification under R8.' Line 19 (R10) covers SMS delivery failure only.

sentence: The finding says no phase check covers plugins/superclaude/commands/; the document already lists this as UNVERIFIED item 8 and has no plugin check in the acceptance tables, which is a missing requirement, not a contradiction or impossible criterion.
evidence: Line 279 (UNVERIFIED item 8): 'How plugins/superclaude/commands/ ... is kept in step with src/superclaude/commands/ ... the update rule ... was not read.' Lines 170-176 (AC-C1 to AC-C5) and 191-210 (phase checks) contain no plugins/ path.
